data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Separation of engines may actually decrease reliability if the checking engine is less capable than the authoring engine, as it may fail to detect subtle errors that the authoring engine 'remembers' making.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The checking engine is of equal or greater capability than the authoring engine.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The error is a 'blind spot' shared by all models of that architecture.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Capability Asymmetry: In cases of high-complexity claims, a weaker 'independent' engine may provide a false positive verification simply due to an inability to parse the error, whereas a stronger single engine acting as a critic can leverage its higher-order reasoning to pinpoint its own failure mode.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
